main_text.l: uidetur. Nam pafsim Hippocrates & Gale-
nus, (quibus maior eft habenda fides, quà
uni Fernelio) & praefertim libro de Natura
Humana, & de Elementis ex ipsius Hippo-
cratis mete similares humani corporis par-
tes ex quatuor humoribus, puta sanguine,
utraq; bile, & pituita proxima materia ori-
ri perspicuè declarant. Nihil praeterea pro-
bat, quod Fernelius ex Galeni libro unde-
cimo Methodi medendi, depromsit, nimi-
rum uirium essentiam in spiritus, carnis &
solidarum partium aequali qualitate, & qua-
litate consistere. His enim tribus substant-
iis, nihil aliud, quà uariis modis uires dis-
solui in diuersis nostri corporis partib. Ga-
lenus nobis significatum uoluit. Quod po-
stremo loco producit Fernelius, uidelicet
relaxantia partis substantiam, statumq;
optimum disipare, morbos materiae mini-
mè probat. Partium namq; robur relaxan-
tia dissoluunt, propterea quod earum tem-
peramentum & structuram labefactant. In-
temperiem enim humidam, & continui dis-
solutionem ipsis partibus inducunt. Si prae-
terea materiae immoderatio esset morbus:
profecto intenderetur ac remitteretur ipsa
materia. Quod sane in rerum natura fieri
nequit:

page.notes: The text is set in a single column; the running head "CAVSAS, PROGYMNASMATA." and page number 79 are printed at the top. The marginal mark "v." in the right margin is a small printed mark, not transcribed as text. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. The printed "dif-" and "po-" hyphens at line ends are kept. "tijs" and "uariis" follow the vowel/consonant rule (j as i). The last word "nequit:" is set right-aligned on its own line, and no catchword is printed.
